title: Finite purely inseparable closures of polynomial rings over normal Japanese domains
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] normal integral domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] which is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. Let $F$ be the fraction field of the polynomial ring $R[x]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], and suppose $F$ has characteristic $p>0$ [def-pc-field-characteristic], where $p$ is prime. Let $L/F$ be a finite purely inseparable field extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Then the integral closure of $R[x]$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $R[x]$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032O (lemma-polynomial-ring-N-2), proof of the second assertion, positive-characteristic argument

proof.text: Apply the coefficient-root cover to obtain a finite coefficient extension E/Frac(R), q>0 and f:L → Frac(A[T]) with X ↦ T^q, where A is the integral closure of R in E. Equip B=A[T] with the R[X]-algebra structure defined by this polynomial substitution. The coefficient maps give an R → R[X] → B scalar tower.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.161.13 (Tag 032O), coefficient-root cover in the second assertion; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032O

proof.text: The Japanese hypothesis gives Module.Finite R A. The integral closure in a finite field extension is normal, and therefore B=A[T] is normal. Since the image of X in B is T^q and q>0, the polynomial variable T is integral over R[X]: its q-th power is in the image of the base ring.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.161.13 (Tag 032O), coefficient-root cover in the second assertion; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032O

proof.text: Choose a finite set of R-algebra generators of A, possible because A is a finite R-module. Map these generators to constant polynomials in B. They are integral over R and hence over R[X]. Adjoin them and T over R[X]; the finite-integral-generators lemma makes this algebra finite. The image of every element of A lies in it, by mapping the original algebra-generator equality and enlarging the base scalars from R to R[X]. Conversely, all polynomial monomials C(a)T^n lie in the algebra generated by the image of A and T; polynomial induction shows that algebra is all of B. The intermediate inclusions are injective maps of modules over the Noetherian ring R[X], so the finite algebra and then B are finite over R[X]. This is the fully proved private helper finite_adjoin_coefficients_and_integral and the polynomial induction in the main proof.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.161.13 (Tag 032O), coefficient-root cover in the second assertion; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032O

proof.text: As B is normal, its integral closure in Frac(B) is B itself, via Mathlib IsIntegralClosure.equiv. It is therefore finite over B, and by transitivity finite over R[X]. The embedding f is an R[X]-algebra map. It maps an integral element over R[X] to an element integral over R[X] and hence over B; restricting its codomain gives an injective linear map from the integral closure of R[X] in L to the integral closure of B in Frac(B). The latter is finite over the Noetherian ring R[X], so Module.Finite.of_injective proves the desired finiteness.
